meetingSpace.interpretationNote: Visually read from the July 2025 meetings brochure capacity grid (page 12) on 2026-10-17. Nobu Ballroom: theatre 500, classroom 220, cabaret (8 per table) 256, boardroom 72, reception 700, reception with dancing 600, dinner (10 per table) 400, dinner dance 330. U-shape and hollow square are blank. Page 7 prose says up to 550 theatre and 250 cabaret. Those two figures conflict with the grid and are not reconciled. Reception of 700 agrees with the hotel website. Ballroom floorplan page states 6,426 sq ft / 597 sq m. Sayuri grid: theatre 45, classroom 24, cabaret 24, boardroom 22, reception 40, dinner '3 rounds - 30 / 1 long - 22', U-shape 20, hollow square 22. Sayuri prose agrees at 22 boardroom or 24 cabaret. Sayuri floorplan: 709 sq ft / 65.9 sq m. Sakura Boardroom grid: boardroom 14 and dinner 16, with other standard sets N/A or blank. Sakura prose says an 18-seat boardroom. That seat count conflicts with the grid value 14. Sakura floorplan: boardroom 532 sq ft / 49.5 sq m; lounge 364 sq ft / 33.9 sq m; lounge reception 16. Mezzanine grid shows reception 200 only. Private Dining Room grid shows dinner 'long table - 20 / rounds - 28'. No single published total meeting-room count or total square footage was summed.

executiveSummary.title: WHAT THE DATA SAYS
executiveSummary.narrative:
Nobu Hotel London Portman Square appeared in at least one AI answer for 47.9% of the traveler needs we tested, showing that AI recognizes the hotel as relevant across a broad range of stays. Across every individual AI answer, however, Nobu Hotel London Portman Square appeared 22.9% of the time. In practical terms, the hotel fits many of the searches being made, but a traveler will not consistently see Nobu Hotel London Portman Square in the hotel options surfaced.

The clearest strength in this period is often placed near the top when ai ranks hotels. See the summary at left for the supporting numbers. Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Nobu Hotel London Portman Square appeared in the Top 3 63.6% of the time, showing how prominently it is positioned when AI includes it.

The main opportunity is consistency: the hotel is already relevant across many traveler needs, so the next focus is understanding where it is absent from individual AI results. No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet, so change over time is not shown.

sections.headline: Nobu Hotel London Portman Square's primary issue is entering AI consideration at all, especially for Adventure & Experiences.
sections.keyInsight: AI Consideration is 22.9%, so the hotel appears in only a limited share of individual comparable responses. When the hotel is absent, Ham Yard Hotel is a leading observed alternative in those gaps — an evidence lead for review, not an automatic proof of recurring substitution. Rank tactics have limited value until relevance improves. The binding constraint is becoming part of the answer set for the traveler needs the hotel currently misses.
sections.whyItMatters: Fine-tuning rank against individual competitors will have limited value until the hotel becomes relevant in more of the traveler needs it currently misses. Entry problems and rank problems require different management attention. If leadership optimizes competitor comparisons first, the hotel can look busy while still missing the larger answer-set gap.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on how the hotel is represented for Adventure & Experiences. Review whether the attributes, positioning, and use cases most relevant to those travelers are complete and consistently represented across priority sources. Treat competitor-rank tactics as secondary until entry improves.
sections.whatToReview: Compare evidence from scenarios where Ham Yard Hotel appears with the property information currently available for Nobu Hotel London Portman Square. Check entry cues first — product type, occasion, and location framing — before broadening the review to secondary attributes.
